beats.line: The control room sees nothing wrong.
The hospital is on diesel. The screens say all is well.

beats.speaker: Raghav Menon
beats.line: Raghav Menon: "My screens say normal, and the city is dark. I need you here."

acts.title: 1. The call
acts.question: What is really on this network?
acts.sceneCue: Three districts dark while the screen inset shows them lit

acts.title: 2. The lie
acts.question: Is the control room seeing the truth?
acts.sceneCue: The split view: the screen on one side, the field on the other

acts.title: 3. The trail
acts.question: Who sent the commands, how did they reach the control room, and what is still running?
acts.sceneCue: Inspect the Network view and Incident Timeline as you prove each lateral hop and decode the implant

acts.title: 4. Shut the doors
acts.question: Can we close the zones without stopping the grid?
acts.sceneCue: Zone walls close while the polling line keeps flowing

acts.title: 5. Lights back
acts.question: Bring the city back safely, then make sure this is caught next time
acts.sceneCue: Districts relight one by one, and the handover goes to Commandant Rathore

opener.speaker: Raghav Menon
opener.line: Three feeders down, hospital on diesel, and my screen says all normal. Tell me what's actually talking out there.

m01.closer: You know who's on the wire. Next: what each signal means.
debriefLines: You confirmed your vantage on the substation network and inventoried the active control and RTU sessions from passive wire captures.
Instead of trusting transport port status alone, you verified live IEC-104 interrogation traffic and located your own read-only frames on the tap.
With every active master and RTU endpoint established, the team can map individual switchyard points without guesswork.
m01.realWorldNote: Before touching relays or firewalls during an OT outage, responders inventory live substation communications passively so active polling is never disrupted.

opener.speaker: Raghav Menon
opener.line: Half our signal sheet was lost in the retrofit. Without it we can't read a single breaker.

m02.closer: The station has a map again. Next: what normal looked like.
debriefLines: You separated the station's authoritative polling stream from a benign secondary monitor and rebuilt the point schedule across all ten controllable assets.
Each breaker, transformer, tie, and generator now has verified status, measurement, and command addresses tied to its owning RTU.
That verified point map makes every forensic log and switching decision downstream traceable to physical switchgear.
m02.realWorldNote: IEC 60870-5-104 point tables are unique to each substation; after hardware retrofits, paper drawings often lag behind live RTU databases.

opener.speaker: Devika Nair
opener.line: I can read you any meter in the yard. Tell me what you expect to see first.

m03.closer: You have a baseline. Next: hold it against the screen.
debriefLines: You audited the pre-incident historian export, removed clock jumps, duplicate timestamps, and sensor spikes, and calculated clean normal electrical readings.
You also queried the DMZ historian read path directly and verified your own request in its access log.
With a clean reference for normal bus voltage, transformer loading, and frequency, subtle manipulation can no longer blend into background noise.
m03.realWorldNote: Indian grid operators track steady-state system frequency against the 49.90 to 50.05 Hz band under CERC Indian Electricity Grid Code 2023 Regulation 30(1).

opener.speaker: Raghav Menon
opener.line: My screen shows the hospital feeder live. Devika is standing next to it and the meter reads zero.

m04.closer: Proven: the screen is lying. Next: who made it lie.
debriefLines: By comparing the control room, the DMZ historian, and the passive field tap, you proved that the operator displays were replaying stale telemetry while suppressing trip events.
You separated deliberate replay timestamp skew from harmless sub-second clock jitter and corroborated the open switchyard bays with Devika's physical panel check.
The substation team now has hard multi-vantage proof that the HMI cannot be trusted until the tampering is found and removed.
m04.realWorldNote: In the December 2015 Ukraine grid outage, the utility's call centre was flooded with fake calls, so the operators could not hear what customers saw. Keeping the operators blind buys time.

opener.speaker: Dr Arvind Kulkarni
opener.line: We have hours of diesel left, not days. I need to know this was deliberate.

m05.closer: You have the commands and where they came from. Next: how they reached the control room.
debriefLines: You isolated the unauthorized IEC-104 control session on the field tap and reconstructed every Select and Execute command pair that opened the tripped feeders.
Contrasting those hostile control frames against your own benign read-only probe established clear protocol proof of deliberate remote switching.
Pairing packet forensics with hospital diesel and water reservoir margins anchored the response around life-safety priorities.
m05.realWorldNote: In April 2022, Industroyer2 sent IEC-104 commands to open breakers at Ukrainian substations. It was caught and stopped before the outage it was set for.

opener.speaker: Raghav Menon
opener.line: Our office network should never reach the control room. Show me how it did.

m06.closer: The path is known. Next: what was left running.
debriefLines: You tied authentication records, cross-zone firewall flows, and host audit trails together to trace the attacker's three-hop lateral pivot across the substation zones.
Inspecting the engineering workstation snapshot revealed the compromised maintenance account and the scheduled persistence entry left behind.
Knowing both the entry path and the persistence mechanism prevents the attacker from simply returning after containment.
m06.realWorldNote: Public post-mortems of the 2015 and 2016 Ukraine grid intrusions documented attackers entering through corporate IT networks and pivoting across jump hosts into substation control environments.

opener.speaker: Raghav Menon
opener.line: Something on the workstation is still feeding the screen old data.

m07.closer: The screen tells the truth again. Next: close the doors without stopping the grid.
debriefLines: You verified the CRC-32 checksum and decoded the binary target configuration left on the engineering workstation, matching its fields against your wire forensics.
Using both your Module 6 persistence path and your decoded checksum, you removed the persistence unit and disabled the telemetry replay shim without interrupting polling.
Control room screens flipped immediately to true open breaker status and real alarms returned to the operator desk.
m07.realWorldNote: Public technical analyses of Industroyer2 described hardcoded per-substation configuration data encoding target RTU addresses, ASDU settings, and breaker IOAs.

opener.speaker: Raghav Menon
opener.line: Lock it down, but if polling stops for even a minute, we're blind again.

m08.closer: Doors shut, polling healthy. Next: bring the city back.
debriefLines: You replaced the permissive inter-zone posture with a default-deny Purdue policy that kept essential substation polling and historian access alive.
You proved containment from the shell with a blocked cross-zone probe and verified a full sixty seconds of uninterrupted post-apply IEC-104 traffic on the passive tap.
With unauthorized conduits sealed and live visibility intact, the switchyard is safe to re-energize.
m08.realWorldNote: Real utilities isolate zones while keeping telemetry alive, because a blind control room is its own outage.

opener.speaker: Harish Verma
opener.line: The pumps need stable voltage to restart. Get it wrong and we trip again.

m09.closer: Suryanagar has power. One job left: make sure this is caught next time.
debriefLines: You calculated each switching step's cold-load surge against this station's seeded ratings and executed controlled two-step switching with critical Tier 1 services first.
Every feeder came back online without tripping overcurrent, voltage, or underfrequency protection, holding cleanly inside the 49.90 to 50.05 Hz band.
Hospital and water works load transferred cleanly off emergency backup, and Suryanagar's districts are lit again.
m09.realWorldNote: After extended outages, substation black-start procedures pace feeder closings carefully because cold-load pickup surges can trip transformers or islanded generators.

opener.speaker: Commandant Vikram Rathore
opener.line: Brief me. What happened, and how will we see it next time?

m10.closer: Handover accepted. Operation Blackout is closed.
debriefLines: You wrote a protocol-invariant IEC-104 detection policy that catches rogue masters, spoofed Originator Addresses, and SBO bypasses across unseen captures with zero false alerts on normal polling.
Your handover brief tied together root cause, compromised credentials, affected bays, containment, operating margin, and residual risks from your own shift evidence.
Commandant Rathore accepted the handover and Suryanagar returns to normal operations with active detection on the field tap.
m10.realWorldNote: Durable OT detection policies validate protocol invariants such as authorized master tuples and Select-Before-Operate state rather than static IP addresses from a single incident.
